name: CA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 district lean combined with Jared Huffman's incumbency since 2013
Republican Robin Littau shows no reported fundraising or outside support
Polymarket prices a Democratic win near 97 percent
Huffman holds roughly $1.1 million in cash on hand
model.rationale: The North Coast district's strong Democratic lean, Huffman's incumbency and million-dollar war chest, and a challenger with no visible fundraising all point to a safe Democratic hold, and prediction markets agree at roughly 97 percent.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal or a late wave of outside spending against Huffman could narrow the margin, and no such signs are present.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's second district runs along the North Coast from Marin County to the Oregon border, and voter registration gives Democrats a double-digit advantage. Jared Huffman has held the seat since 2013 and advanced to the general election as expected. He reports about $1 million in cash on hand, while Republican Robin Littau shows no reported fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets price a Huffman win around 97 percent. The expected margin sits in the low twenties, matching the district's partisan lean plus a typical incumbent edge. Barring an unforeseen development, this ranks among the safest Democratic House seats on the ballot.
